html:
Jassim bin Mohammed Al Thani was the ruler of Qatar from 1878 to 1913, remembered as the founder of the modern state. Qatar's national day, 18 December, marks his accession.

His father had made the Al Thani the leading family of the peninsula, with British recognition in 1868. Jassim moved Qatar out of the shadow of Bahrain and its Al Khalifa rulers. He accepted Ottoman protection for a time, then turned on the Ottomans when they tried to tax and garrison the country, beating them at the Battle of Al Wajbah in 1893.

He kept Qatar's pearling towns united under one family. His heirs signed a treaty of protection with Britain in 1916 and ruled on into the oil age (Qatar).
